quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective riding gear?
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a leather jacket, sturdy pants, boots that cover your ankles, and hearing protection. Soft material pants do not provide protection.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend
Keep your friend busy with other activities
Stop your friend from leaving until they are sober
Let your friend ride their motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Let your friend ride their motorcycle
questions.explanation: Never allow a friend to ride their motorcycle after drinking. Instead, arrange a safe ride home, keep them busy, ask them to stay until they are sober, or get help from other friends.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust your mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and the lane next to you.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield
Does not protect as well as goggles

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handgrip. Know where all your controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: What happens if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: The ride will feel too smooth

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield
Does not protect as well as goggles

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: What is the danger of a skidding rear tire?

options.text: It only matters if the front tire is also skidding

questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. When the rear wheel locks, you lose the ability to change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: How do you maintain control while turning your motorcycle?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn

questions.explanation: To maintain control through a turn, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid accidents?

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you very closely
Look only at your controls and not ahead
Signal your intentions to other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers
questions.explanation: To reduce accidents, be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your plans. Keep space around your motorcycle and always look ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press the rear brake pedal. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: You can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy. Your motorcycle needs more distance to stop on wet roads.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, all riders should stop. Hand signals are important for group riding communication.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you maximum stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position you should always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and not dangerous. Relax and ride straight ahead at a steady speed. Do not weave—this will make the problem worse.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting to first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down before downshifting into a lower gear. If you downshift while going too fast, your motorcycle may lurch and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, the riders should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders at once.

questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. The next rider should only begin passing after the previous rider has completed their pass.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the sign then proceed through.
Ignore the sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the sign, then edge forward to check for cross traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the sign, then edge forward to check for cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line first. Then edge forward and stop again near the crossroad. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: When a rider extends their left arm straight out to the left, what does it mean?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals when they don't have turn signals. An extended left arm means the rider is turning left or changing lanes to the left.

questions.question: What is another name for shifting to a lower gear?
questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it slows the motorcycle similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What do studies show about motorcycles with headlights on during the day?

options.text: They are harder to see than other vehicles.
Other drivers notice them more than when the headlight is off.
They are less safe than when the headlight is off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers notice them more than when the headlight is off.
questions.explanation: Keeping your headlight on while riding makes your motorcycle more visible. A motorcycle with its headlight on during the day is twice as likely to be seen by other drivers.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: Only experienced riders should use it.
Use it alone without the rear brake.
Use it occasionally to help the rear brake.
Use it together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent serious injury?
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not protect you from injury.
